raw_segments.text: Capitation taxes, if it is attempted to proportion them to the fortune or revenue of each contributor,
The state of a man's fortune varies from day to day,
and without an inquisition, more intolerable than any tax,
and renewed at least once every year, can only be guessed at.
His assessment, therefore, must, in most cases,
depend upon the good or bad humor of his assessors,
and must, therefore, be altogether arbitrary and uncertain.
